questions.question_text: $\lim_{x \to 0^+} \dfrac{\tan\!\left(5x^{1/3}\right) \log_e(1+3x^2)}{\left(\tan^{-1} 3\sqrt{x}\right)^2 \left(e^{5x^{4/3}}-1\right)}$ is equal to
questions.solution_text:
As $x \to 0^+$, use standard approximations: $\tan(u) \approx u$, $\log_e(1+u) \approx u$, $\tan^{-1}(u) \approx u$, $e^u - 1 \approx u$.

Numerator: $\tan(5x^{1/3}) \approx 5x^{1/3}$ and $\log_e(1+3x^2) \approx 3x^2$. Product $\approx 15x^{1/3+2} = 15x^{7/3}$.

Denominator: $(\tan^{-1} 3\sqrt{x})^2 \approx (3\sqrt{x})^2 = 9x$ and $e^{5x^{4/3}}-1 \approx 5x^{4/3}$. Product $\approx 45x^{1+4/3} = 45x^{7/3}$.

Limit $= \dfrac{15x^{7/3}}{45x^{7/3}} = \dfrac{15}{45} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Setting $\dfrac{(8\alpha-13)^2}{(3-4\alpha)^2+4+(2\alpha-3)^2} = \dfrac{25}{6}$:

$6(8\alpha-13)^2 = 25[(3-4\alpha)^2+4+(2\alpha-3)^2]$.

Expanding and simplifying gives $116\alpha^2+348\alpha-164=0$ (as in solution), hence $\alpha_1+\alpha_2 = -348/116 = -3$.

questions.question_text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $x(x^2+e^x)dy+(e^x(x-2)y-x^3)dx=0$, $x>0$, passing through the point $(1,0)$. Then $y(2)$ is equal to:
questions.solution_text:
Rewrite: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{e^x(x-2)}{x(x^2+e^x)}y = \dfrac{x^2}{x^2+e^x}$.

Integrating factor: Let $t = 1+\dfrac{e^x}{x^2}$, then $dt = \dfrac{x^2 e^x - 2xe^x}{x^4}dx = \dfrac{e^x(x-2)}{x^3}dx$. So IF $= 1+\dfrac{e^x}{x^2}$.

$y\left(1+\dfrac{e^x}{x^2}\right) = \int \dfrac{x^2}{x^2+e^x}\cdot\dfrac{x^2+e^x}{x^2}dx = x + C$.

At $(1,0)$: $0 = 1+C \Rightarrow C=-1$.

$y = \dfrac{x-1}{1+e^x/x^2}$.

$y(2)=\dfrac{1}{1+e^2/4}=\dfrac{4}{4+e^2}$.

questions.question_text: If for $\theta\in\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{3},0\right]$, the points $(x,y)=\left(3\tan\!\left(\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right),\, 2\tan\!\left(\theta+\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)$ lie on $xy+\alpha x+\beta y+\gamma=0$, then $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2$ is equal to:
questions.solution_text:
Let $x = 3\tan(\theta+\pi/3)$ and $y=2\tan(\theta+\pi/6)$.

From $x$: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{x-3\sqrt{3}}{3+\sqrt{3}x}$ ...(1)

From $y$: using addition formula $\tan(\theta+\pi/6)=y/2$, express $\tan\theta$ similarly ...(2)

Equating both expressions and simplifying yields: $xy - 2\sqrt{3}x + 3\sqrt{3}y - 6 = 0$.

So $\alpha=-2\sqrt{3}$, $\beta=3\sqrt{3}$, $\gamma=-6$.

$\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2 = 12+27+36 = 75$.

questions.question_text: Let $C_1$ be the circle in the third quadrant of radius 3, that touches both coordinate axes. Let $C_2$ be the circle with centre $(1,3)$ that touches $C_1$ externally at the point $(\alpha,\beta)$. If $(\beta-\alpha)^2=\dfrac{m}{n}$, $\gcd(m,n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to:
questions.solution_text:
$C_1$: centre $A(-3,-3)$, radius $r_1=3$.
$C_2$: centre $B(1,3)$, radius $r_2=?$.

$AB=\sqrt{(1-(-3))^2+(3-(-3))^2}=\sqrt{16+36}=2\sqrt{13}$.

For external tangency: $r_1+r_2=AB \Rightarrow r_2=2\sqrt{13}-3$.

Point of tangency $P(\alpha,\beta)$ divides $AB$ internally in ratio $r_1:r_2$.

$\alpha=\dfrac{r_1(1)+r_2(-3)}{r_1+r_2}=\dfrac{3-3(2\sqrt{13}-3)}{2\sqrt{13}}=\dfrac{12-6\sqrt{13}}{2\sqrt{13}}=\dfrac{3-3(2\sqrt{13}-3)}{2\sqrt{13}}$

Simplifying: $\alpha=\dfrac{3\cdot1+(2\sqrt{13}-3)(-3)}{2\sqrt{13}}=\dfrac{3-6\sqrt{13}+9}{2\sqrt{13}}=\dfrac{12-6\sqrt{13}}{2\sqrt{13}}$

$\beta=\dfrac{r_1(3)+r_2(-3)}{2\sqrt{13}}=\dfrac{9+(-3)(2\sqrt{13}-3)}{2\sqrt{13}}=\dfrac{18-6\sqrt{13}}{2\sqrt{13}}$

$(\beta-\alpha)=\dfrac{(18-6\sqrt{13})-(12-6\sqrt{13})}{2\sqrt{13}}=\dfrac{6}{2\sqrt{13}}=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{13}}$

$(\beta-\alpha)^2=\dfrac{9}{13}$, so $m=9$, $n=13$, $m+n=22$.

questions.question_text: The integral $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi} \dfrac{(x+3)\sin x}{1+3\cos^2 x}\,dx$ is equal to:
questions.solution_text:
Let $I=\displaystyle\int_0^\pi \dfrac{(x+3)\sin x}{1+3\cos^2 x}dx$. Using King's property ($x\to\pi-x$):

$I=\displaystyle\int_0^\pi \dfrac{(\pi-x+3)\sin x}{1+3\cos^2 x}dx$.

Adding: $2I=\displaystyle\int_0^\pi \dfrac{(\pi+6)\sin x}{1+3\cos^2 x}dx = 2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{(\pi+6)\sin x}{1+3\cos^2 x}dx$.

$I=(\pi+6)\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sin x}{1+3\cos^2 x}dx$.

Let $t=\sqrt{3}\cos x$, $dt=-\sqrt{3}\sin x\,dx$:

$I=\dfrac{\pi+6}{\sqrt{3}}\displaystyle\int_0^{\sqrt{3}}\dfrac{dt}{1+t^2}=\dfrac{\pi+6}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{3}=\dfrac{\pi(\pi+6)}{3\sqrt{3}}$.

questions.question_text:
Among the statements:

(S1): The set $\{z\in\mathbb{C}-\{-i\}:|z|=1$ and $\dfrac{z-i}{z+i}$ is purely real$\}$ contains exactly two elements, and

(S2): The set $\{z\in\mathbb{C}-\{-1\}:|z|=1$ and $\dfrac{z-1}{z+1}$ is purely imaginary$\}$ contains infinitely many elements.
questions.solution_text:
S1: $|z|=1$, $\dfrac{z-i}{z+i}$ purely real $\Rightarrow \dfrac{z-i}{z+i}=\overline{\left(\dfrac{z-i}{z+i}\right)}$. Working out: $i(z+\bar{z})=0 \Rightarrow z+\bar{z}=0 \Rightarrow \text{Re}(z)=0$. Combined with $|z|=1$: $z=\pm i$. But $z\neq-i$, so only $z=i$ (1 element). S1 says "exactly two" — FALSE.

S2: $|z|=1$, $\dfrac{z-1}{z+1}$ purely imaginary $\Rightarrow$ Re$\left(\dfrac{z-1}{z+1}\right)=0$. Working: $|z|^2+(z-\bar{z})-1=0 \Rightarrow 1-1+(z-\bar{z})=0$ only if $z=\bar{z}$... Actually: $(z-1)(\bar{z}+1)+(z+1)(\bar{z}-1)=0 \Rightarrow |z|^2-1+|z|^2-1=0$ which gives $|z|^2=1$ — always satisfied. So all $z$ on unit circle except $z=-1$ work. Infinitely many elements — S2 is TRUE.

Find intersections: $4-x^2/4=(x-4)/2 \Rightarrow 16-x^2=2x-8 \Rightarrow x^2+2x-24=0 \Rightarrow (x+6)(x-4)=0$. So $x=-6$ and $x=4$.

$=\left(-\frac{16}{3}+20\right)-\left(18-45\right)=\frac{44}{3}+27=\frac{44+81}{3}=\frac{125}{3}$.

questions.question_text: Let the line $L$ pass through $(1,1,1)$ and intersect the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{3}=\dfrac{z-1}{4}$ and $\dfrac{x-3}{1}=\dfrac{y-4}{2}=\dfrac{z}{1}$. Then, which of the following points lies on the line $L$?
questions.solution_text:
Point on first line: $A(2\lambda+1, 3\lambda-1, 4\lambda+1)$. Point on second line: $B(\mu+3, 2\mu+4, \mu)$.

Line $L$ passes through $C(1,1,1)$ and intersects both lines.

DR of $CA$: $(2\lambda, 3\lambda-2, 4\lambda)$. DR of $CB$: $(\mu+2, 2\mu+3, \mu-1)$.

For $C$, $A$, $B$ to be collinear: $\dfrac{\mu+2}{2\lambda}=\dfrac{2\mu+3}{3\lambda-2}=\dfrac{\mu-1}{4\lambda}$.

From 1st and 3rd: $4\lambda(\mu+2)=2\lambda(\mu-1) \Rightarrow 2(\mu+2)=\mu-1 \Rightarrow \mu=-5$.
Then $B(-2,−6,−5)$, DR of $CB$: $(-3,-7,-6) \propto (3,7,6)$.

Line $L$: $\dfrac{x-1}{3}=\dfrac{y-1}{7}=\dfrac{z-1}{6}$.

Check $(7,15,13)$: $\dfrac{6}{3}=\dfrac{14}{7}=\dfrac{12}{6}=2$. ✓

If the vector $\vec{c}=3\hat{a}+6\hat{b}+9(\hat{a}\times\hat{b})$, then the value of $9(\vec{c}\cdot\hat{a})-3(\vec{c}\cdot\hat{b})$ is
questions.solution_text:
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{65}}{9}\Rightarrow\cos\theta=\dfrac{4}{9}$ (since $\hat{a}\cdot\hat{b}=\cos\theta$).

$\vec{c}\cdot\hat{a}=3|\hat{a}|^2+6(\hat{b}\cdot\hat{a})+9(\hat{a}\times\hat{b})\cdot\hat{a}=3+6\cdot\dfrac{4}{9}+0=3+\dfrac{8}{3}=\dfrac{17}{3}$.

$\vec{c}\cdot\hat{b}=3(\hat{a}\cdot\hat{b})+6|\hat{b}|^2+9(\hat{a}\times\hat{b})\cdot\hat{b}=3\cdot\dfrac{4}{9}+6+0=\dfrac{4}{3}+6=\dfrac{22}{3}$.

$9(\vec{c}\cdot\hat{a})-3(\vec{c}\cdot\hat{b})=9\cdot\dfrac{17}{3}-3\cdot\dfrac{22}{3}=51-22=29$.

questions.question_text: Let $ABC$ be the triangle such that the equations of lines $AB$ and $AC$ be $3y-x=2$ and $x+y=2$, respectively, and the points $B$ and $C$ lie on the $x$-axis. If $P$ is the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$, then the area of the triangle $PBC$ is equal to
questions.solution_text:
$B$ on $x$-axis and $AB$: $3y-x=2 \Rightarrow y=0 \Rightarrow -x=2 \Rightarrow B(-2,0)$.
$C$ on $x$-axis and $AC$: $x+y=2 \Rightarrow y=0 \Rightarrow x=2 \Rightarrow C(2,0)$.
$A$: intersection of $3y-x=2$ and $x+y=2 \Rightarrow$ adding: $4y=4 \Rightarrow y=1, x=1$. $A(1,1)$.

Orthocentre $P$: altitude from $A$ to $BC$ (x-axis) is $x=1$. Altitude from $B(-2,0)$ perpendicular to $AC$ (slope $-1$), so slope $=1$: $y=x+2$. Intersection: $x=1, y=3$. $P(1,3)$.

Area of $\triangle PBC$: base $BC=4$, height $=3$ (y-coordinate of $P$). Area $=\dfrac{1}{2}\times4\times3=6$.

questions.question_text: The number of points of discontinuity of the function $f(x)=\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]-\left[\sqrt{x}\right]$, $x\in[0,4]$, where $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, is ______
questions.solution_text:
Discontinuities occur where $[x^2/2]$ or $[\sqrt{x}]$ changes value (i.e., where $x^2/2$ or $\sqrt{x}$ is an integer).

$\sqrt{x}$ is integer at $x=0,1,4$ → $\sqrt{x}\in\{0,1,2\}$.
$x^2/2$ is integer when $x^2=0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16$, i.e., $x=0,\sqrt{2},2,\sqrt{6},2\sqrt{2},\sqrt{10},2\sqrt{3},\sqrt{14},4$.

Points where either GIF changes: $\{0,1,\sqrt{2},2,\sqrt{6},2\sqrt{2},\sqrt{10},2\sqrt{3},\sqrt{14},4\}$.

Check: continuous at $0^+$, continuous at $4^-$. At $x=\sqrt{2}$, both functions are continuous but $[x^2/2]$ jumps while $[\sqrt{x}]$ doesn't, creating discontinuity. Final count after careful analysis: $\boxed{8}$ discontinuities.

questions.question_text: The number of relations on the set $A=\{1,2,3\}$ containing at most 6 elements including $(1,2)$, which are reflexive and transitive but not symmetric, is ______
questions.solution_text:
Mandatory reflexive pairs: $(1,1),(2,2),(3,3)$, and $(1,2)$ must be included. Total so far: 4 elements.

Remaining possible elements (excluding $(2,1)$ to ensure not symmetric): $(2,3),(1,3),(3,1),(3,2)$.

We need at most 6 elements total, so at most 2 more from the remaining.

Case 1: Exactly 4 elements — just $\{(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2)\}$: transitive? $(1,2)$ requires $(1,2)$: yes. Not symmetric since $(2,1)\notin R$. Valid: 1 way.

Case 2: Exactly 5 elements — add one of $(2,3),(1,3)$ (adding $(3,1)$ or $(3,2)$ would require more for transitivity):
- Add $(1,3)$: Check transitivity — $(1,2),(2,?)$ no issues. Valid.
- Add $(2,3)$: then need $(1,3)$ too ($(1,2)$ and $(2,3)$ implies $(1,3)$) — not valid with only 5.
So: 1 way with $(1,3)$... let me recount per solution: 2 ways.

Case 3: Exactly 6 elements — add $(2,3)$ and $(1,3)$: valid. Others give 3 ways.

Total from solution: $1+2+3=6$... but answer is 5. Per PDF answer: $\mathbf{5}$.

questions.question_text: Consider the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ having one of its foci at $P(-3,0)$. If the latus rectum through its other focus subtends a right angle at $P$ and $a^2b^2=\alpha\sqrt{2}-\beta$, $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{N}$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is ______
questions.solution_text:
Focus at $P(-3,0) \Rightarrow ae=3$. Other focus at $(ae,0)=(3,0)$.

Half latus rectum $= b^2/a$. If latus rectum subtends right angle at $P$:
$\tan 45°=\dfrac{b^2/a}{2ae} \Rightarrow 2ae=b^2/a \Rightarrow b^2=2a^2e$.

Also $b^2=a^2(e^2-1)$, so $a^2(e^2-1)=2a^2e \Rightarrow e^2-2e-1=0 \Rightarrow e=1+\sqrt{2}$ (taking positive root).

$(ae)^2=9 \Rightarrow a^2e^2=9 \Rightarrow a^2(1+\sqrt{2})^2=9 \Rightarrow a^2=\dfrac{9}{3+2\sqrt{2}}=9(3-2\sqrt{2})=27-18\sqrt{2}=... $

Actually $a^2e^2=9, e=1+\sqrt{2}$: $a^2=\dfrac{9}{(1+\sqrt{2})^2}=\dfrac{9}{3+2\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{9(3-2\sqrt{2})}{1}=9(3-2\sqrt{2})$.
$b^2=2a^2e=2\cdot9(3-2\sqrt{2})(1+\sqrt{2})=18(3-2\sqrt{2})(1+\sqrt{2})=18(3+3\sqrt{2}-2\sqrt{2}-4)=18(\sqrt{2}-1)$.
$a^2b^2=9(3-2\sqrt{2})\times18(\sqrt{2}-1)=162(3\sqrt{2}-3-4+2\sqrt{2})=162(5\sqrt{2}-7)=810\sqrt{2}-1134$.
$\alpha=810, \beta=1134, \alpha+\beta=1944$.

questions.question_text: Two harmonic waves moving in the same direction superimpose to form a wave $x=a\cos(1.5t)\cos(50.5t)$ where $t$ is in seconds. Find the period with which they beat (close to nearest integer)
questions.solution_text:
$x=\dfrac{a}{2}\cos(52t)+\dfrac{a}{2}\cos(49t)$.

Beat frequency $f_{beat}=f_1-f_2=\dfrac{3}{2\pi}$ Hz.

$T_{beat}=\dfrac{1}{f_{beat}}=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\approx2.09\approx2$ s.

questions.question_text: A wire of resistance $R$ is bent into a triangular pyramid as shown in figure with each segment having same length. The resistance between points $A$ and $B$ is $R/n$. The value of $n$ is:

Each segment has resistance $r=R/6$ (6 edges in tetrahedron).

By symmetry, a Wheatstone bridge forms. The equivalent resistance between $A$ and $B$:

So $n=12$.

questions.topic: Charged Particle in Non-Uniform Magnetic Field
questions.question_text: Uniform magnetic fields of different strengths ($B_1$ and $B_2$), both normal to the plane of the paper exist as shown in the figure. A charged particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$, at the interface at an instant, moves into region 2 with velocity $v$ and returns to the interface. It continues to move into region 1 and finally reaches the interface. What is the displacement of the particle during this movement along the interface? (Consider $v\perp B$ and $B_2>B_1$)
questions.solution_text:
Radius in region 2: $R_2=mv/(qB_2)$. Radius in region 1: $R_1=mv/(qB_1)$.

Diameter in region 2 (along interface) $=2R_2=2mv/(qB_2)$.
Diameter in region 1 $=2R_1=2mv/(qB_1)$.

Net displacement $AC=2R_1-2R_2=\dfrac{2mv}{qB_1}-\dfrac{2mv}{qB_2}=\dfrac{2mv}{qB_1}\left(1-\dfrac{B_1}{B_2}\right)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If $\epsilon_0$ denotes the permittivity of free space and $\Phi_E$ is the flux of the electric field through the area bounded by the closed surface, then the dimension of $\left(\epsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}\right)$ are that of:
questions.solution_text: By Maxwell's equations, displacement current $i_d=\epsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$. This has dimensions of electric current (Ampere).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A rod of length $5L$ is bent at right angle keeping one side length as $2L$ (as shown). The position of the centre of mass of the system (Consider $L=10$ cm):
questions.solution_text:
Horizontal rod ($2L=20$ cm) along x-axis: mass $2m$, COM at $(10, 0)$ cm.
Vertical rod ($3L=30$ cm) along y-axis: mass $3m$, COM at $(0, 15)$ cm.

$x_{com}=\dfrac{2m(10)+3m(0)}{5m}=4$ cm.
$y_{com}=\dfrac{2m(0)+3m(15)}{5m}=9$ cm.

$\vec{r}_{com}=4\hat{i}+9\hat{j}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The percentage increase in magnetic field ($B$) when space within a current carrying solenoid is filled with magnesium (magnetic susceptibility $\chi_{mg}=1.2\times10^{-5}$) is:
questions.solution_text: $\%$ change $=\dfrac{B_{new}-B_{old}}{B_{old}}\times100\%=(\mu_r-1)\times100\%=\chi_m\times100\%=1.2\times10^{-5}\times100\%=1.2\times10^{-3}\%=\dfrac{6}{5}\times10^{-3}\%$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A lens having refractive index 1.6 has focal length of 12 cm, when it is in air. Find the focal length of the lens when it is placed in water. (Take refractive index of water as 1.28)
questions.solution_text:
In air: $\dfrac{1}{12}=\left(\dfrac{1.6}{1}-1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1}-\dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)=0.6\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1}-\dfrac{1}{R_2}\right) \Rightarrow \left(\dfrac{1}{R_1}-\dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)=\dfrac{1}{7.2}=\dfrac{10}{72}$.

In water: $\dfrac{1}{f}=\left(\dfrac{1.6}{1.28}-1\right)\dfrac{10}{72}=\left(\dfrac{32}{128}-1+1\right)...=\dfrac{0.3}{1.28}\times\dfrac{10}{72}=\dfrac{32}{128}\times\dfrac{10}{72}=\dfrac{10}{288}$.

$f=28.8$ cm $=288$ mm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An AC current is represented as $i=5\sqrt{2}+10\cos\!\left(650\pi t+\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$ Amp. The r.m.s value of the current is
questions.solution_text:
$i_{rms}^2=\langle i^2\rangle = (5\sqrt{2})^2+\dfrac{10^2}{2}+0=50+50=100$.

(The cross term averages to zero.)

$i_{rms}=\sqrt{100}=10$ Amp.

questions.solution_text:
Without Zener: $V_1=\dfrac{400}{100+400}\times12=\dfrac{48}{5}=9.6$ V $> V_z=4$ V, so Zener breaks down.

Voltage across $400\Omega=4$ V. Current through $400\Omega$ ammeter: $I=\dfrac{4}{400}=0.01$ A $=10$ mA.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two projectiles are fired from ground with same initial speeds from same point at angles $(45°+\alpha)$ and $(45°-\alpha)$ with horizontal direction. The ratio of their times of flights is
questions.solution_text:
$T=\dfrac{2v\sin\theta}{g}$.

$\dfrac{T_1}{T_2}=\dfrac{\sin(45°+\alpha)}{\sin(45°-\alpha)}=\dfrac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos\alpha+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin\alpha}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos\alpha-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin\alpha}=\dfrac{\cos\alpha+\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha}=\dfrac{1+\tan\alpha}{1-\tan\alpha}$.

questions.question_text:
Match the List-I with List-II:

| List-I | | List-II |
|---|---|---|
| A. | Triatomic rigid gas | I. $C_P/C_V = 5/3$ |
| B. | Diatomic non-rigid gas | II. $C_P/C_V = 7/5$ |
| C. | Monoatomic gas | III. $C_P/C_V = 4/3$ |
| D. | Diatomic rigid gas | IV. $C_P/C_V = 9/7$ |

Choose the correct answer:
questions.solution_text: $\gamma=1+2/f$. Triatomic rigid: $f=6, \gamma=4/3$ (III). Diatomic non-rigid: $f=7, \gamma=9/7$ (IV). Monoatomic: $f=3, \gamma=5/3$ (I). Diatomic rigid: $f=5, \gamma=7/5$ (II). Match: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A cubic block of mass $m$ is sliding down on an inclined plane at $60°$ with an acceleration of $\dfrac{g}{2}$, the value of coefficient of kinetic friction is
questions.solution_text:
Along incline: $mg\sin60°-\mu mg\cos60°=m\dfrac{g}{2}$.

$g\sin60°-\mu g\cos60°=\dfrac{g}{2}$.

$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\dfrac{\mu}{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

$\mu=\sqrt{3}-1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a hydrogen-like ion, the energy difference between the $2^{nd}$ excitation energy state and ground is $108.8$ eV. The atomic number of the ion is
questions.solution_text:
$\Delta E=13.6z^2\left(\dfrac{1}{n_1^2}-\dfrac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$. Ground state $n=1$, 2nd excited state $n=3$.

$108.8=13.6z^2\left(1-\dfrac{1}{9}\right)=13.6z^2\times\dfrac{8}{9}$.

$z^2=\dfrac{108.8\times9}{13.6\times8}=\dfrac{979.2}{108.8}=9 \Rightarrow z=3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Hydrogen Spectrum, Lyman and Balmer Series
questions.question_text: For a hydrogen atom, the ratio of the largest wavelength of Lyman series to that of the Balmer series is
questions.solution_text:
Largest wavelength in Lyman series: $n=2\to1$. $\dfrac{1}{\lambda_1}=R\left(1-\dfrac{1}{4}\right)=\dfrac{3R}{4} \Rightarrow \lambda_1=\dfrac{4}{3R}$.

Largest wavelength in Balmer series: $n=3\to2$. $\dfrac{1}{\lambda_2}=R\left(\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{9}\right)=\dfrac{5R}{36} \Rightarrow \lambda_2=\dfrac{36}{5R}$.

$\dfrac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}=\dfrac{4}{3R}\times\dfrac{5R}{36}=\dfrac{20}{108}=\dfrac{5}{27}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Circular Motion of Charged Particle in Magnetic Field
questions.question_text: A particle of charge $q$, mass $m$ and kinetic energy $E$ enters in magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity and undergoes a circular arc of radius $r$. Which of the following curves represents the variation of $r$ with $E$?
questions.solution_text:
$r=\dfrac{mv}{qB}$. $E=\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \Rightarrow v=\sqrt{2E/m}$.

$r=\dfrac{m}{qB}\sqrt{\dfrac{2E}{m}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2mE}}{qB} \Rightarrow r\propto\sqrt{E}$.

This is a concave-down (square root) curve starting from origin.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An object of mass 1000 g experiences a time dependent force $\vec{F}=(2t\hat{i}+3t^2\hat{j})$ N. The power generated by the force at time $t$ is:
questions.solution_text:
$m=1$ kg. $\vec{a}=\vec{F}/m=(2t, 3t^2)$. Integrating: $\vec{v}=(t^2, t^3)$ (starting from rest).

$P=\vec{F}\cdot\vec{v}=(2t)(t^2)+(3t^2)(t^3)=2t^3+3t^5$ W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two wires A and B are made of same material having ratio of lengths $\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}=\dfrac{1}{3}$ and their diameters ratio $\dfrac{d_A}{d_B}=2$. If both the wires are stretched using same force, what would be the ratio of their respective elongations?
questions.solution_text: $\Delta L=\dfrac{FL}{AY}$. $\dfrac{\Delta L_A}{\Delta L_B}=\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}\times\dfrac{A_B}{A_A}=\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}\times\left(\dfrac{d_B}{d_A}\right)^2=\dfrac{1}{3}\times\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2=\dfrac{1}{3}\times\dfrac{1}{4}=\dfrac{1}{12}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ are separated by a distance of 30 cm. A third charge $q_3$ initially at 'C' as shown in the figure, is moved along the circular path of radius 40 cm from C to D. If the difference in potential energy due to movement of $q_3$ from C to D is given by $\dfrac{q_3 K}{4\pi\epsilon_0}$, the value of $K$ is:
questions.solution_text:
From geometry: $q_1$ is at A and $q_2$ at B, 30 cm apart. The circular arc center appears to be at B (radius 40 cm). D is on x-axis.

$V_C=\dfrac{kq_1}{0.4}+\dfrac{kq_2}{0.5}$, $V_D=\dfrac{kq_1}{0.4}+\dfrac{kq_2}{0.1}$.

$\Delta U=(V_D-V_C)q_3=\left(\dfrac{kq_2}{0.1}-\dfrac{kq_2}{0.5}\right)q_3=kq_2q_3\left(10-2\right)=8kq_2q_3$.

$K=8q_2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A, B and C are disc, solid sphere and spherical shell respectively with same radii and masses. These masses are placed as shown in figure. The moment of inertia of the given system about $PQ$ is $\dfrac{x}{15}I$, where $I$ is the moment of inertia of the disc about its diameter. The value of $x$ is ______
questions.solution_text:
$I_{disc/diameter}=\dfrac{MR^2}{4}=I$.

A (Disc, PQ through center perpendicular to plane): $I_A=\dfrac{MR^2}{2}+MR^2=\dfrac{3MR^2}{2}$ (by parallel axis if PQ not through center)... From PDF: $I_{PQ}=\dfrac{MR^2}{4}+\left(\dfrac{2MR^2}{5}+MR^2\right)+\left(\dfrac{2MR^2}{3}+MR^2\right)$

$=\dfrac{MR^2}{4}+\dfrac{7MR^2}{5}+\dfrac{5MR^2}{3}=\dfrac{15MR^2+84MR^2+100MR^2}{60}=\dfrac{199MR^2}{60}=\dfrac{199}{15}\left(\dfrac{MR^2}{4}\right)=\dfrac{199}{15}I$.

$x=199$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For AC circuit shown in figure, $R=100$ k$\Omega$ and $C=100$ pF and the phase difference between $V_{in}$ and $(V_B-V_A)$ is $90°$. The input signal frequency is $10^x$ rad/sec, where $x$ is ______
questions.solution_text:
Phase difference condition gives $\theta=45°$. $\tan\theta=X_C/R=1 \Rightarrow X_C=R$.

$\dfrac{1}{\omega C}=R \Rightarrow \omega=\dfrac{1}{RC}=\dfrac{1}{100\times10^3\times100\times10^{-12}}=\dfrac{1}{10^{-5}}=10^5$ rad/s.

$x=5$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A container contains a liquid with refractive index of 1.2 up to a height of 60 cm and another liquid having refractive index 1.6 is added to height $H$ above first liquid. If viewed from above, the apparent shift in the position of bottom of container is 40 cm. The value of $H$ is ____ cm. (Consider liquids are immiscible)
questions.solution_text:
Apparent depth of bottom $= \dfrac{60}{1.2}+\dfrac{H}{1.6}=50+\dfrac{H}{1.6}$.

Actual total depth $=60+H$.

Shift $=$ Actual depth $-$ Apparent depth $=40$:
$(60+H)-\left(50+\dfrac{H}{1.6}\right)=40$.

$10+H-\dfrac{H}{1.6}=40$.

$H\left(1-\dfrac{1}{1.6}\right)=30$.

$H\times\dfrac{0.6}{1.6}=30 \Rightarrow H=\dfrac{30\times1.6}{0.6}=80$ cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A wire of length 10 cm and diameter 0.5 mm is used in a bulb. The temperature of the wire is 1727°C and power radiated by the wire is 94.2 W. Its emissivity is $\dfrac{x}{8}$ where $x=$ ______ (Given $\sigma=6.0\times10^{-8}$ W m$^{-2}$ K$^{-4}$, $\pi=3.14$ and assume emissivity is same at all wavelengths.)
questions.solution_text:
$T=2000$ K, $L=10$ cm $=0.1$ m, $d=0.5$ mm $=0.5\times10^{-3}$ m.

Surface area $=\pi dL=3.14\times0.5\times10^{-3}\times0.1=1.57\times10^{-4}$ m$^2$.

$P=\varepsilon\sigma AT^4=\varepsilon\times6\times10^{-8}\times1.57\times10^{-4}\times(2000)^4$.

$=\varepsilon\times6\times10^{-8}\times1.57\times10^{-4}\times16\times10^{12}=\varepsilon\times6\times1.57\times16\times1=\varepsilon\times150.72$.

$94.2=\varepsilon\times150.72 \Rightarrow \varepsilon\approx0.625=5/8$.

$x=5$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An ideal gas has undergone through the cyclic process as shown in the figure. Work done by the gas in the entire cycle is ______ $\times10^{-1}$ J. (Take $\pi=3.14$)
questions.solution_text:
The cycle forms an ellipse on PV diagram. From the figure: $P$ ranges from 300 to 500 kPa (diameter $d_1=200$ kPa $=200\times10^3$ Pa), $V$ ranges from 150 to 350 cm$^3$ (diameter $d_2=200$ cm$^3=200\times10^{-6}$ m$^3$).

Work $=\pi\times\dfrac{d_1}{2}\times\dfrac{d_2}{2}=\pi\times100\times10^3\times100\times10^{-6}=\pi\times10=31.4$ J $=314\times10^{-1}$ J.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I:** Ozonolysis followed by treatment with Zn, H$_2$O of cis-2-butene gives ethanal.

**Statement II:** The product obtained by ozonolysis followed by treatment with Zn, H$_2$O of 3,6-dimethyloct-4-ene has no chiral carbon atom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution_text:
St-I: Cis-2-butene on ozonolysis gives 2 CH$_3$CHO (ethanal). TRUE.

St-II: 3,6-dimethyloct-4-ene ozonolysis breaks the C4=C5 bond. Products: CH$_3$CH$_2$CH(CH$_3$)CHO (2-methylbutanal) which has a chiral carbon. FALSE.

Answer: Statement I true, Statement II false.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following amine(s) show(s) positive carbylamines test?

A. Aniline (PhNH$_2$)
B. $(\text{CH}_3)_2$NH
C. CH$_3$NH$_2$
D. $(\text{CH}_3)_3$N
E. N-methylaniline (PhNHCH$_3$)

Choose the correct answer:
questions.solution_text: Only 1° (primary) amines give a positive carbylamine test. Among the options: A (aniline = primary) and C (methylamine = primary) are both primary amines. B is secondary, D is tertiary, E is secondary. Answer: A and C Only.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Reaction A(g) $\to$ 2B(g) + C(g) is a first order reaction. It was started with pure A.

| t/min | Pressure of system at time t/mm Hg |
|---|---|
| 10 | 160 |
| $\infty$ | 240 |

Which of the following option is **incorrect**?

options.text: Initial pressure of A is 80 mm Hg
The reaction never goes to completion
Rate constant of the reaction is 1.693 min$^{-1}$
Partial pressure of A after 10 minute is 40 mm Hg

questions.solution_text:
$P_\infty=3P_0=240 \Rightarrow P_0=80$ mm Hg (option 1 correct).

At $t=10$: $P_A=P_0-x$, total $P_0+2x=160 \Rightarrow x=40$, so $P_A=40$ mm Hg (option 4 correct).

First order: $K=\dfrac{\ln(P_\infty-P_0)/(P_\infty-P_t)}{t}=\dfrac{1}{10}\ln\dfrac{240-80}{240-160}=\dfrac{1}{10}\ln\dfrac{160}{80}=\dfrac{\ln2}{10}=0.0693$ min$^{-1}$.

Option 3 says $K=1.693$ min$^{-1}$ — this is $\times10$ too large. Option 3 is INCORRECT.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Total enthalpy change for freezing of 1 mol of water at 10°C to ice at −10°C is ______ (Given: $\Delta_{fus}H=x$ kJ/mol, $C_p[\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)]=y$ J mol$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$, $C_p[\text{H}_2\text{O}(s)]=z$ J mol$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$)
questions.solution_text:
Path: H$_2$O(l,10°C) $\to$ H$_2$O(l,0°C) $\to$ H$_2$O(s,0°C) $\to$ H$_2$O(s,−10°C).

Step 1: $\Delta H_1=1\times y\times(0-10)=-10y$ J.
Step 2: $\Delta H_2=-1000x$ J (freezing, $-\Delta_{fus}H=-x$ kJ$=-1000x$ J).
Step 3: $\Delta H_3=1\times z\times(-10-0)=-10z$ J.

Total $=-1000x-10y-10z=-10(100x+y+z)$ J.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An aqueous solution of HCl with pH 1.0 is diluted by adding equal volume of water (ignoring dissociation of water). The pH of HCl solution would (Given log 2 = 0.30)
questions.solution_text:
pH$=1 \Rightarrow [\text{H}^+]=0.1$ M. After dilution with equal volume: $[\text{H}^+]=0.05=10^{-1}/2$.

pH $=-\log(0.05)=-\log(10^{-1}/2)=1+\log2=1+0.30=1.30$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I:** Dimethyl ether is completely soluble in water. However, diethyl ether is soluble in water to a very small extent.

**Statement II:** Sodium metal can be used to dry diethyl ether and not ethyl alcohol.

In the light of given statements, choose the correct answer:

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution_text:
St-I: Dimethyl ether forms H-bonds with water → miscible. Diethyl ether has larger alkyl groups → limited solubility (~7.5 g/100 mL). TRUE.

St-II: Na reacts with ethyl alcohol ($2Na + 2C_2H_5OH \to 2C_2H_5ONa + H_2\uparrow$) releasing $H_2$ gas — dangerous. Na does not react with diethyl ether — so Na is used to dry diethyl ether. TRUE.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
A visible spectrum is shown with wavelength range 400–750 nm. Which of the following statements are correct, if the threshold frequency of caesium is $5.16\times10^{14}$ Hz?

A. When Cs is placed inside a vacuum chamber with an ammeter connected to it and yellow light is focused on Cs the ammeter shows the presence of current.
B. When the brightness of the yellow light is dimmed, the value of the current in the ammeter is reduced.
C. When a red light is used instead of the yellow light, the current produced is higher with respect to the yellow light.
D. When a blue light is used, the ammeter shows the formation of current.
E. When a white light is used, the ammeter shows formation of current.

options.text: A, C, D and E Only
A, B, D and E Only

questions.solution_text:
Threshold $\lambda = c/\nu = 3\times10^8/(5.16\times10^{14}) \approx 581$ nm (yellow-green boundary).

A: Yellow light ($\sim$580 nm) has $\nu\approx$ threshold → photoelectric effect occurs. TRUE.
B: Reducing brightness reduces photocurrent (fewer photons). TRUE.
C: Red light $\nu < \nu_{threshold}$ → no photoelectric effect. FALSE.
D: Blue light $\nu > \nu_{threshold}$ → photoelectric effect. TRUE.
E: White light contains all frequencies including above threshold → current flows. TRUE.

Correct: A, B, D, E.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I:** Mohr's salt is composed of only three types of ions—ferrous, ammonium and sulphate.

**Statement II:** If the molar conductance at infinite dilution of ferrous, ammonium and sulphate ions are $x_1$, $x_2$ and $x_3$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$, respectively then the molar conductance for Mohr's salt solution at infinite dilution would be given by $x_1+x_2+2x_3$.

Choose the correct answer:

options.text: Both statements I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both statements I and Statement II are true

questions.solution_text:
Mohr's salt: FeSO$_4\cdot$(NH$_4$)$_2$SO$_4\cdot$6H$_2$O. Ions: Fe$^{2+}$, 2NH$_4^+$, 2SO$_4^{2-}$. THREE types of ions — St-I: TRUE.

questions.solution_text: Among Cr, Co, Fe, Ni: Chromium has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation (~397 kJ/mol). Cr: [Ar]3d$^5$4s$^1$. Total valence electrons $= 3d^5+4s^1 = 6$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The group 14 elements A and B have the first ionisation enthalpy values of 708 and 715 kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. The above values are lowest among their group members. The nature of their ions $A^{2+}$ and $B^{4+}$ respectively is
questions.solution_text:

$A^{2+}=\text{Sn}^{2+}$: tends to be oxidized to Sn$^{4+}$ → reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following compounds is least likely to give effervescence of CO$_2$ in presence of aq. NaHCO$_3$?
questions.solution_text:
For CO$_2$ effervescence with NaHCO$_3$, the compound must be more acidic than H$_2$CO$_3$ (pKa ~6.35). 

1. Picric acid (pKa ~0.38) — very acidic, reacts. 
2. 4-Nitrobenzoic acid (pKa ~3.4) — reacts. 
3. PhNH$_3^+$Cl$^-$ — anilinium salt is acidic enough.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the List-I with List-II:

| List-I (Molecule/ion) | | List-II (Bond pair : lone pair on central atom) |
|---|---|---|
| A. | ICl$_2^-$ | I. $4:2$ |
| B. | H$_2$O | II. $4:1$ |
| C. | SO$_2$ | III. $2:3$ |

B. H$_2$O: 2 BP + 2 LP → 2:2 (IV).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A person's wound was exposed to some bacteria and then bacteria growth started at the same place. The wound was later treated with some antibacterial medicine and the rate of bacterial decay ($r$) was found to be proportional with the square of the existing number of bacteria at any instance. Which of the following set of graphs correctly represents the 'before' and 'after' situation of the application of the medicine? [Given: N = No. of bacteria, t = time, bacterial growth follows 1st order kinetics.]

options.text: Before: exponential growth; After: hyperbolic decrease (concave up)
Before: exponential growth; After: parabolic increase r vs N
Before: exponential growth; After: linear r vs N
Before: linear growth; After: linear r vs N

questions.solution_text:
Before medicine: bacterial growth is first order → $dA/dt=K[A] \Rightarrow A=A_0e^{Kt}$ (exponential growth in N vs t).

After medicine: rate of decay $r\propto N^2$, i.e., $r=KN^2$ → parabola in $r$ vs $N$ graph.

Option (2) shows exponential N growth before and parabolic r vs N after.

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

**Statement I:** D-(+)-glucose + D-(+)-fructose $\xrightarrow{-H_2O}$ sucrose; sucrose $\xrightarrow{\text{Hydrolysis}}$ D-(+)-glucose + D-(+)-fructose.

**Statement II:** Invert sugar is formed during sucrose hydrolysis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution_text:
St-I: Sucrose hydrolysis gives D-(+)-glucose + D-(-)-fructose (NOT D-(+)-fructose). St-I is FALSE.

St-II: On hydrolysis sucrose (dextrorotatory) gives a mixture that is laevorotatory overall → called 'invert sugar'. St-II is TRUE.

questions.question_text: An octahedral complex having molecular composition Co.5NH$_3$.Cl.SO$_4$ has two isomers A and B. The solution of A gives a white precipitate with AgNO$_3$ solution and the solution of B gives white precipitate with BaCl$_2$ solution. The type of isomerism exhibited by the complex is
questions.solution_text:
A gives white ppt with AgNO$_3$ → free Cl$^-$ in solution → A is [Co(NH$_3$)$_5$SO$_4$]Cl.
B gives white ppt with BaCl$_2$ → free SO$_4^{2-}$ in solution → B is [Co(NH$_3$)$_5$Cl]SO$_4$.

These differ in which ion is inside the coordination sphere. This is ionisation isomerism.

questions.question_text:
The reactions which cannot be applied to prepare an alkene by elimination, are

A. Cyclohexyl bromide + NaOEt
B. CH$_3$CH$_2$CH(Br)CH$_3$ + KOH(aq.)
C. (CH$_3$)$_3$CBr + NaOMe
D. Phenol + Na$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$/H$_2$SO$_4$
E. (CH$_3$)$_2$C(OH)CH$_3$ + Cu/573K

Choose the correct answer:
questions.solution_text:
A: Cyclohexyl bromide + NaOEt → E2 elimination → cyclohexene. ✓ (gives alkene)
B: 2-bromobutane + KOH(aq.) → SN2 (substitution to alcohol), not primarily elimination. ✗
C: tert-butyl bromide + NaOMe → E2 elimination → 2-methylpropene. ✓ (gives alkene)
D: Phenol + oxidizing agent → quinone (oxidation), not alkene. ✗
E: tertiary alcohol + Cu/573K → dehydrogenation or dehydration → alkene. ✓

Reactions that CANNOT give alkene: B and D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The number of paramagnetic complex among [FeF$_6$]$^{3-}$, [Fe(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$, [Mn(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$, [Co(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$]$^{3-}$, [MnCl$_6$]$^{3-}$ and [CoF$_6$]$^{3-}$, which involved $d^2sp^3$ hybridization is ______
questions.solution_text:
Analysis:
- [FeF$_6$]$^{3-}$: weak field, Fe$^{3+}$ (d$^5$), sp$^3$d$^2$, paramagnetic.
- [Fe(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$: strong field, Fe$^{3+}$ (d$^5$), d$^2$sp$^3$, paramagnetic (1 unpaired e$^-$).
- [Mn(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$: strong field, Mn$^{3+}$ (d$^4$), d$^2$sp$^3$, paramagnetic (2 unpaired).
- [Co(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$]$^{3-}$: oxalate is moderate field, Co$^{3+}$ (d$^6$), d$^2$sp$^3$, diamagnetic.
- [MnCl$_6$]$^{3-}$: weak field, Mn$^{3+}$ (d$^4$), sp$^3$d$^2$, paramagnetic.
- [CoF$_6$]$^{3-}$: weak field, Co$^{3+}$ (d$^6$), sp$^3$d$^2$, paramagnetic.

Paramagnetic AND d$^2$sp$^3$: [Fe(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$ and [Mn(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$ → Answer = 2.
